f.modes: Use `A` to append at the end of a line and `O` to open a line above, instead of moving first and then pressing `i`.
f.undo: After an undo, `Ctrl-r` redoes it; you never need to retype what you just undid.
m.word: Reach for `w`, `b` and `e` before holding `l`: one key per word instead of one per character.
m.WORD: `W` and `B` skip over punctuation like `foo.bar(baz)` in one hop.
m.line: `^` lands on the first non-blank character, which is where you usually want to be in indented code.
m.find: `f(` jumps straight to the opening parenthesis of a call on the current line.
m.repeatfind: After `f,`, press `;` to hop to the next comma instead of typing `f,` again.
m.count: Put a count before a motion: `3w` moves three words in two keystrokes.
m.file: `gg` and `G` jump to the start and end of the file; `42G` goes straight to line 42.
m.para: `}` jumps to the next blank line, which in most code means the next function or block.
m.rel: Turn on `relativenumber` and jump to any visible line with `{count}j` or `{count}k`.
m.match: Press `%` on a bracket to jump to its partner, handy for finding the end of a long call.
m.search: `/name<CR>` is often the fastest way to reach a line you cannot see.
m.star: `*` searches for the word under the cursor; then `n` walks through every use.
o.delete: `D` deletes to the end of the line; `dw` and `d$` compose with any motion.
o.change: `cw` replaces a word and leaves you in insert mode, saving a separate `dw` and `i`.
o.yank: `yiw` copies the word under the cursor without moving to its start first.
o.dot: Make an edit once, then press `.` on the next spot: the cheapest repeat in Vim.
o.indent: `>ip` indents the whole paragraph; `=ip` re-indents it.
o.case: `gUiw` uppercases the word under the cursor, great for constants.
o.join: `J` joins the next line onto this one with a single space.
o.number: `Ctrl-a` increments the number under (or after) the cursor; `5Ctrl-a` adds five.
t.word: `ciw` changes the whole word from anywhere inside it.
t.quote: `ci"` changes a string's contents from anywhere inside the quotes.
t.paren: `ci(` rewrites all the arguments of a call in one go.
t.bracket: `di[` empties a list or index expression without touching the brackets.
t.brace: `di{` clears the body of a block or object literal.
t.tag: `cit` changes the text inside an HTML or JSX tag.
t.para: `yap` copies a whole paragraph or function, including the trailing blank line.
t.compose: Think in verb plus noun: `da(`, `yi"`, `>ip` all work the same way.
v.line: `V` then `j`/`k` selects whole lines; `>` indents the selection.
v.block: `Ctrl-v` selects a column; it is Vim's native multi-cursor.
v.blockedit: `Ctrl-v`, select lines, `$A;<Esc>` appends a semicolon to every line.
v.reselect: `gv` reselects the last visual selection, so you can apply a second operator.
r.named: `"ayy` yanks into register a; `"ap` pastes it back even after other yanks.
r.yank0: `"0p` pastes what you last yanked, even after `dd` overwrote the default register.
r.insert: In insert mode, `Ctrl-r 0` pastes your last yank without leaving insert.
x.subst: `:%s/old/new/g` renames every occurrence in the file at once.
x.lastsearch: Search with `/foo`, then `cgn` and `.` to change matches one at a time.
x.global: `:g/pattern/d` deletes every line that matches, in one command.
x.normal: `:'<,'>normal A;` appends a semicolon to every selected line.
x.copymove: `:m+1` moves the current line down one; `:t.` duplicates it.
a.dot: Design edits to be repeatable: `A;<Esc>` then `j.` beats editing each line by hand.
a.macro: Record with `qa`, stop with `q`, replay with `@a`, then `@@` to repeat.
n.marks: `ma` sets a mark; `'a` jumps back to that line from anywhere in the file.
n.jumplist: `Ctrl-o` takes you back to where you were before a jump or search.
n.lastinsert: `gi` resumes inserting exactly where you last left insert mode.
n.unmatched: `[{` jumps to the start of the enclosing block from anywhere inside it.
i.delete: In insert mode, `Ctrl-w` deletes the previous word without leaving insert.
i.oneshot: `Ctrl-o` runs one normal-mode command and drops you back into insert.
i.escape: `Ctrl-[` leaves insert mode without reaching for the Escape key.
nv.comment: `gcc` toggles a comment on the current line; `gcip` comments a paragraph.
